cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives cashless hospital coverage up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year. It pays for doctor visits, medicines, tests, surgery, ICU, implants, room and food. It also covers three days before and fifteen days after hospitalisation, all pre‑existing diseases from day one, and has no limit on family size or location.
cards.who_can_apply: Rural families that meet any one of the listed deprivation criteria such as living in a kutcha house, having no adult aged 16 to 59, having a disabled member without an able‑bodied adult, being SC/ST, landless manual labourers, or without shelter can apply. Urban workers in eleven occupational groups like ragpickers, domestic workers, street vendors, construction labourers, sweepers, home‑based artisans, transport workers, shop assistants, electricians, mechanics and washer‑men can also apply.
cards.documents: Age and identity proof such as Aadhaar or PAN card, proof of address, and income or caste certificate are needed. The family’s ration card or other family ID is also required. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit a hospital or Community Service Centre. Give the operator your PM letter, RSBY URN or mobile number. The Arogya Mitra will search the database, verify your Aadhaar and ration card, upload scanned documents and, after approval, issue an e‑card for you and your family.

cards.benefit_text: When you turn 60 you will get a guaranteed pension of Rs. 1000 per month or Rs. 2000 per month or Rs. 3000 per month or Rs. 4000 per month or Rs. 5000 per month for life. If you die, your spouse gets the same pension. After both die, the nominee receives the saved pension wealth.
cards.who_can_apply: You must be between 18 and 40 years old to join. There is no income limit to join. You must have a savings bank or post office account for auto‑debit of contributions.
cards.documents: Aadhaar card, bank or post office passbook, nominee details form The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Log in to your internet banking or visit the eNPS website, choose Atal Pension Yojana, fill basic and nominee details, give consent for auto‑debit, and complete KYC using Aadhaar OTP, virtual ID or upload Aadhaar XML.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme brings one member, preferably a woman, from each rural poor household into a Self Help Group network with bank linkage. SHGs are federated to give voice, resources and reduce external dependence. It supports social mobilisation, financial inclusion, livelihood promotion, skill development for rural youth, revolving funds, interest subvention and convergence with other poverty programmes.
cards.who_can_apply: Any active Self Help Group that has existed for at least six months can apply. The group must follow the Panchasutras of regular meetings, savings, inter‑loaning, timely repayment and keep up‑to‑date books. Defunct SHGs can also apply if revived and active for three months. No age or income limits are set.
cards.documents: Aadhar Number, Proof of Identity, Proof of Residence, Voter ID Card, Passport Size Photo The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Go online to the DAY‑NRLM registration page. Fill in name, email, contact number, choose a username, create and confirm a password, then click Create New Account.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives a short‑term credit limit for the first year based on the crop finance scale, plus 10% for post‑harvest needs, 20% for repairs, and insurance. In later years the limit adds 10% for cost escalation and includes a term‑loan component for up to five years, forming the maximum permissible limit.
cards.who_can_apply: Farmers who own cultivations can apply. Tenant farmers, oral lessees and share croppers are also eligible. Groups of farmers such as SHGs or JLGs can apply as well. There is no age or income rule specified.
cards.documents: Application form, two passport size photographs, ID proof like Aadhar or voter ID, address proof, certified landholding proof, cropping pattern details, security documents if loan exceeds Rs.1.60 lakhs or Rs.3.00 lakhs. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the bank’s website, choose Kisan Credit Card and click Apply. Fill the online form with required details and submit. You will receive a reference number and the bank will contact you within a few working days. You may also apply offline at the bank branch.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme provides apprenticeship training in Designated Trades for one year for ITI pass‑outs and two years for fresher or non‑ITI candidates, and in Optional Trades for six, nine or twelve months. The government pays 25% of the stipend, up to ₹1,500 per month, directly to the apprentice’s bank account. Minimum monthly stipend starts at ₹5,000 for school pass‑outs and goes up to ₹9,000 for graduate apprentices.
cards.who_can_apply: Anyone aged 14 years or more can apply, and the upper age limit is 35 years. For designated trades in hazardous industries, the minimum age is 18 years. There is no income condition. Candidates must have an Aadhaar number and complete e‑KYC on the apprenticeship portal.
cards.documents: Aadhaar Card. Documents required as per the selected trade. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the Apprenticeship Portal at apprenticeshipindia.gov.in. Click Login/Register and choose Candidate. Enter mobile number, email and Aadhaar to complete e‑KYC. Verify with OTP. After registration you can apply for the apprenticeship.

cards.benefit_text: Farmers get financial assistance of ₹6,000 per year in three equal installments of ₹2,000 every four months.
cards.who_can_apply: Any farmer family that owns cultivable land in its name can apply. There is no age limit and no income limit mentioned in the scheme.
cards.documents: Aadhaar Card, landholding papers, savings bank account statement. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the PM‑Kisan portal online. Choose New Farmer Registration, enter your Aadhaar and mobile number, verify with OTP, fill the details, upload the required documents and submit.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives a working capital loan up to ₹15,000 for the first tranche, up to ₹25,000 for the second, and up to ₹50,000 for the third. Interest is subsidised at 7% per year and credited quarterly. A digital transaction cashback of up to ₹100 per month is offered. A credit guarantee covers 31.87% of the first tranche, 8.25% of the second and 6% of the third. After repaying the second tranche, a UPI linked RuPay credit card with an initial limit of ₹10,000, extendable to ₹30,000, is provided.
cards.who_can_apply: Street vendors who have a Certificate of Vending or Identity Card issued by the Urban Local Body can apply. Vendors identified in the survey but not yet issued a certificate can also apply. Vendors left out of the survey or who started vending later can apply if they have a Letter of Recommendation from the ULB or Town Vending Committee.
cards.documents: Certificate of Vending, Identity Card, Letter of Recommendation, Aadhaar Card, Survey Reference Number (SRN) The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in and click Log In. Enter your mobile number, request the OTP and log in. Select your vendor category, enter the mandatory Survey Reference Number, fill the online form, upload the required documents and submit.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives financial assistance of ₹ 1,20,000 per unit for plain areas and ₹ 1,30,000 per unit for hilly, difficult areas and IAP districts. A beneficiary can get a loan of up to ₹ 70,000 at 3% lower interest and a subsidy on a principal of up to ₹ 2,00,000. It also gives up to ₹ 12,000 for toilet construction, a LPG connection, and employment as a rural mason at ₹ 90.95 per day for 95 days.
cards.who_can_apply: Households without any shelter, living on alms, manual scavengers, primitive tribal groups and legally released bonded laborers are included. The scheme also targets families living in zero, one or two room kutcha houses. Eligibility does not depend on age or income.
cards.documents: Aadhaar number and self‑attested copy of the Aadhaar card, Job Card registered with MGNREGA, Bank account details, Swachh Bharat Mission number, and an affidavit stating the family does not own a pucca house. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the official PMAY‑G website and log in. Fill personal details, upload the Aadhaar consent form and search for your name. Register by selecting ‘Select to Register’, then add bank details, loan choice, MGNREGA job card number and SBM number as prompted.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives a margin‑money subsidy for new micro‑enterprises. General category applicants pay 10% of project cost and receive 15% subsidy in urban areas, 25% in rural areas. Special category applicants pay 5% and receive 25% subsidy in urban areas, 35% in rural areas. Upgrading existing units gets 10% contribution and 15% subsidy, 20% in NER and hill states.
cards.who_can_apply: Any individual aged 18 years or older can apply. There is no income ceiling. For projects over Rs.10 lakh in manufacturing or Rs.5 lakh in business/service, a minimum VIII standard education is required. Existing subsidised units are not eligible.
cards.documents: Caste Certificate, Project Report, Education or skill development training certificate The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the official PMEGP website. Click the Apply button under the appropriate tab for new or existing units. Fill in the online form, upload the required documents, and submit the application.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme offers low premiums. Farmers pay up to 2% for Kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food and oilseed crops, and 5% for commercial or horticultural crops. The government subsidises the rest, and in North‑Eastern States, Jammu, Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh it pays the whole premium. It covers natural disasters, pests, diseases, post‑harvest losses and localised calamities, and processes claims within two months after harvest.
cards.who_can_apply: All farmers, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers, who grow notified crops in notified areas can apply. Applicants must have an insurable interest in the crops, a valid land ownership certificate or land tenure agreement, and must be the cultivator or sharecropper on the insured land. Applications should be made within two weeks of the sowing season start.
cards.documents: Passport‑sized photograph, identity proof such as Aadhaar or voter ID, address proof like electricity bill, evidence of land records such as land possession certificate, and a declaration about the crop sown. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the official PMFBY website and click Farmer Corner, then Guest Farmer to register. Fill in personal, residential, ID and bank details, and submit the form. Log in with your mobile number, fill the application form, upload the documents and submit. Choose Pay Later or make payment, then track the status online.

cards.benefit_text: The scheme gives Shishu loans up to Rs.50,000, Kishore loans above Rs.50,000 up to Rs.5 lakh, Tarun loans above Rs.5 lakh up to Rs.10 lakh, and Tarun Plus loans up to Rs.20 lakh for entrepreneurs who have repaid previous Tarun loans.
cards.who_can_apply: Any individual, proprietary concern, partnership firm, private limited company, public company or other legal form can apply. The applicant should not be a defaulter and must have a satisfactory credit track record. The borrower may need the necessary skills or experience for the proposed activity.
cards.documents: Proof of identity (Voter ID, PAN, Aadhaar, etc.), proof of residence (recent utility bill or similar), recent coloured photograph, proof of identity/address of the business enterprise, and statement of accounts for the last six months if loan is Rs.2 lakh or above. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Go to the PM Mudra official website and select the Udyamimitra portal. Click “Apply Now”, enter name, email and mobile number and generate OTP. Then fill personal and business details, choose the loan category, attach the required documents and submit the application.

cards.benefit_text: Farmers get subsidies of 50 to 80 percent when they buy agricultural machinery, making the equipment cheaper. The scheme also promotes custom hiring centres and develops hubs for high‑tech farm equipment, helping farmers work faster and increase yield.
cards.who_can_apply: All landholding farmers and their families, SHGs, user groups, cooperative societies, FPOs and entrepreneurs can apply. The farmer must be a native of India and financially weak. Women farmers get priority and anyone who has not taken another central subsidy earlier can apply.
cards.documents: Aadhar card, Record of Right of land, copy of first page of bank pass book, passport size photo, any ID proof such as Driving licence or Voter ID. The CSC centre will tell you the full list of papers.
cards.how_to_apply: Visit the portal agrimachinery.nic.in, choose the registration option, fill the form with correct district, block and personal details, and submit the application online.
